== Course of events ==

The Mouse begins telling his personal history to Alice—a confession more intimate than the English history he had recited earlier, though that tale too had been riddled with interruptions from the assembled animals. Yet as he speaks of his 'long tail', Alice somehow misunderstands him entirely. This small error proves fateful. The Mouse, wounded by Alice's misinterpretation, becomes angry at once. His indignation admits no remedy; he storms away, abandoning his narrative and leaving Alice bereft of his company.

With the Mouse departed, Alice finds herself once more alone in Wonderland, set adrift to pursue whatever strange encounters the land might offer next.
